definition_of_ayu.english: Life is the combination of body (śarīra), sense organs (indriya), mind (sattva/manas), and soul (ātma). As long as these four are combined, life exists.

synonyms.dharī: That which prevents the body from decay
synonyms.nityagam: That which serves as permanent substratum of the body
synonyms.anubandham: That which transmigrates from one body to another

definition_of_ayurveda.english: The science or knowledge of life. Āyu = life; vetti = science or knowledge.

definition_of_health.english: Equilibrium state of the three doṣas (vāta, pitta, kapha) along with seven dhātus, three malas, and power of digestion, combined with pleasant mind, soul, and sense organs.

samsarga.definition: Vitiation of any 2 doṣas (either vṛddhi or kṣaya)

vata.primary_site: Below the navel region (pakwashaya — large intestine)
vata.agni_effect: Viṣamāgni — unsteady or erratic digestive activity

pitta.primary_site: Between the heart and umbilicus (āmāshaya — small intestine region)

reasoning.lakshana: Color resembles lotus flower, lac, and insect indragopa
reasoning.kriya: Supporting life and nourishing the body

rakta_dosha_debate.AH_conclusion: Rakta cannot be called a doṣa — it is itself vitiated by the three doṣas, not vitiating others. The doṣas are three only.
rakta_dosha_debate.flag: NOTE: Cross-reference with Caraka Saṃhitā on rakta classification

manasika_doshas.note: Sattva is not a doṣa — it is conductive to health. Rajas and Tamas cause psychological disorders.

prakriti_system.definition: Constitution of the body formed at the time of union of spermatozoa and ovum, based on dominant doṣa at that time.
prakriti_system.analogy: Like poisonous worms developing from poisonous material — the dominant doṣa at conception determines constitution.

dhatu_system.definition: Dhātus support the body throughout life. They get vitiated by the three doṣas and are called dūṣyas.

dhatus.function_english: Satisfaction to the mind and nourishing the body

dhatu_system.nourishment_principle: Each dhātu divides into 3 parts: (1) nourishes its own tissue, (2) nourishes the next succeeding dhātu as food, (3) becomes waste product.

vriddhi_kshaya_principle.vriddhi: Intake of food with similar qualities causes increase in corresponding dhātu/doṣa
vriddhi_kshaya_principle.kshaya: Intake of food with opposite qualities causes decrease

types.name: Dravya sāmānya
types.example: Intake of mutton increases muscle tissue (similar substance)

types.name: Guṇa sāmānya
types.example: Sweet and heavy substances increase kapha (similar qualities)

types.name: Karma viśeṣa
types.example: Excessive exercises leads to kapha kṣaya

mala_system.definition: Three waste products of the body. Also vitiated by the three doṣas.

rasa_system.definition: Rasa is the taste perceived by the tongue. In Ayurveda 6 tastes are described.
rasa_system.strength_order: Madhura > Amla > Lavaṇa > Tikta > Kaṭu > Kaṣāya (decreasing strength)

virya_system.definition: Potency (vīrya) which exists in a substance, based on dominancy of qualities.

vipaka_system.definition: After completion of digestion, substances are converted into one of 3 post-digestive tastes. This transformation process is vipāka.

types.name: Madhura vipāka
types.effect: Generally increases Kapha; decreases Vāta and Pitta

gurvadi_dravya_gunas.note: Also called dwandwa guṇas — 10 pairs of opposites

special_gunas.vyavayi: Spreads all over the body initially; undergoes digestion later
special_gunas.vikasi: Harms the tissues of the body and causes loosening of joints
special_gunas.note: These are associated with sara (mobile) and tīkṣṇa (sharp) guṇas respectively

example_samana_applications.ghrita: Reduces pitta due to madhura rasa and other guṇas
example_samana_applications.honey: Reduces kapha due to astringent taste and dryness
example_samana_applications.milk_fish_combination: Increases doṣas due to incompatibility (viruddha āhāra)
healthy_food_staples: Milk — suitable for maintenance of positive health

asatmyendriyartha_samyoga.hinayoga: Insufficient use — not hearing, seeing, tasting, smelling, touching
asatmyendriyartha_samyoga.mithyayoga: Wrong use — seeing unnatural objects, hearing harsh sounds, smelling putrefying odours
asatmyendriyartha_samyoga.atiyoga: Excessive use — very bright objects, very loud sounds, powerful pungent smells

prajnaparadha.hinayoga: Not doing physical, mental or vocal activities
prajnaparadha.mithyayoga: Suppressing natural urges, falling from height, unusual activities
prajnaparadha.atiyoga: Excessive exercise, coitus, riding, talking, thinking

parinama_kala.hinayoga: Less heat in summer, less cold in winter than normal
parinama_kala.mithyayoga: Cold in summer and heat in winter (reversed seasons)
parinama_kala.atiyoga: More heat in summer and more cold in winter than normal

nija_rogas.mechanism: Irregular diet and activities → doṣa vitiation first → then signs and symptoms appear

agantuja_rogas.mechanism: Ābhighāta (accident/external trauma) → signs and symptoms first → then doṣa vitiation

yapya.description: Patient survives only by continuously following wholesome regimen. Flares with slightest unwholesome regimen. Death is certain but time is prolonged.

good_prognosis_factors: Body capable of withstanding all types of treatments
Causes, prodromal symptoms and signs are mild and devoid of complications
Doṣa, dūṣya, deśa, kāla and prakṛti are all dissimilar
Fourfold therapeutic measures available with beneficial planetary constellations
Only one doṣa involved in pathogenesis, manifested in one pathway
bad_prognosis_factors: Requires more than one difficult treatment method (medicine + surgery + alkalines + cauterization)

varjaniya_roga_lakshana.title: Signs of diseases to be rejected for treatment
signs: Exact opposite qualities of curable diseases
Involved in vital tissues and organs

varjaniya_rogi_lakshana.title: Patients to be discarded for treatment
signs: Lacking equipment and instruments for proper treatment
Busily engaged in other activities; not paying attention to treatment
Violent, grief-ridden, fearful, ungrateful, self-diagnosing patients

ideal_qualities: Śuci — purity in acts of mind, body and speech
bhishak.importance: Most important among the four limbs — even with other limbs lacking, an efficient physician can manage treatment

ideal_qualities: Bahukalpam — capable of multiple pharmaceutical preparations (swarasa, kalka, cūrṇa, kwātha etc.)
Bahuguṇam — highest number of guṇas; can be used across many conditions by altering anupāna
Sampannam — potent and free from infection and moisture
Yogyam — suitable to patient and disease per region and season
Anurakta — utmost affection and service motto toward patient
Śuci — physical and psychological purity; devotion and dedication
Dakṣatā — perfectly trained; skilled in nursing
Āḍhya — wealthy (able to procure required equipment and drugs)
Jñāpaka — good memory to narrate medical history
Sattvavān — strong will power; can tolerate difficult situations

sodhana.mechanism: Eliminates vitiated doṣas from body using Pañcakarma

samana.limitation: Prone to relapse as doṣas may be re-aggravated

pratahkala_utthana.title: Wake-up Time
significance: All three doṣas are in equilibrium state at this time
Suitable for study and obtaining knowledge
pratahkala_utthana.note: Unhealthy or diseased persons are NOT required to wake early; they follow the physician's instructions.

shauca_vidhi.title: Morning Cleansing
method: Assess body condition (check if previous night's food has been fully digested)
Attend to natural urges (faeces and urine)
rules: Face north in morning hours; face south in night hours
During defecation: be silent, sit, cover head with cloth
Avoid defecating at dirty places, centre of road, heaps of ash, cowshed, burial grounds, sacred places, in front of women or respectable persons, facing sun or moon
At time of urge, do not attend any other work
shauca_vidhi.contraindication_note: Suppressing natural urges leads to vitiation of Vāta, causing many diseases.
shauca_vidhi.exceptions: Sick persons or persons in fear may void as they wish.

danta_dhavana.title: Danta-Dhāvana — Teeth Cleaning

herbs_recommended.safety_flag: Generally safe for oral use in small amounts
⚠️ CONTAINS CARDIAC GLYCOSIDES — toxic if ingested. Oral use only with extreme caution. Cross-check with Caraka Saṃhitā.

danta_dhavana.timing: Early morning and immediately after food
danta_dhavana.method: Without causing pain or injury to the gums
danta_dhavana.order: Brush lower row of teeth first, then upper row

tooth_powder_formula_astanga_sangraha.vehicle: Madhu (honey) — mix fine powders with honey to prepare paste
tooth_powder_formula_astanga_sangraha.method: Use paste with twig for rubbing; do not injure gums

flags_and_contradictions.detail: Nerium indicum contains cardiac glycosides and is potentially toxic if ingested. Listed in AH for oral use as a tooth-cleaning twig. Cross-reference with Caraka Saṃhitā and Bhāvaprakāśa before including in any VEDA oral health recommendation.
flags_and_contradictions.action: VERIFY before UI display to users

flags_and_contradictions.detail: AH concludes rakta is NOT a doṣa. Some other ācāryas categorize it as 4th doṣa. Caraka Saṃhitā to be checked for authoritative position.
flags_and_contradictions.action: Prioritize Caraka Saṃhitā per VEDA hierarchy

flags_and_contradictions.detail: Chapter 2 data is partial (pages 26–29 only). Remainder of Dinacaryā continues in next chunk. Do not use Dinacaryā data as complete until merged.
AH Ch.5 describes honey as yogavāhī (anusṇa-anasīta — neither hot nor cold). Some texts assign mild uṣṇa vīrya. Caraka Saṃhitā and Bhāvaprakāśa to be checked for authoritative virya classification.
flags_and_contradictions.action: Prioritize Caraka Saṃhitā per VEDA hierarchy

flags_and_contradictions.topic: Buttermilk (Takra) types — Dalhana vs. Dhanvantari Nighantu
flags_and_contradictions.detail: Dalhana commentary gives 3 types based on butter content; Dhanvantari Nighantu gives 4 types (Ghola, Mathita, Udasvit, Takra) based on water ratio. Both sourced through this AH translation. Record both versions.
flags_and_contradictions.action: Record both in database with source annotation; display clinical version

flags_and_contradictions.topic: Honey + Heat — Toxicity Exception for Panchakarma
flags_and_contradictions.detail: AH categorically states heated honey is toxic/poison-like. However, the same chapter permits heated honey in therapeutic vamana and vasti procedures where it exits the body quickly without undergoing digestion. This is NOT a contradiction but a clinical exception — must be documented accurately.
flags_and_contradictions.action: In VEDA UI: label heated honey as contraindicated with pop-up exception note for Panchakarma context

flags_and_contradictions.topic: Non-classical publisher insert — Gomūtra newspaper clipping
flags_and_contradictions.detail: Page 33 of the Ashtanga Hrdayam PDF contains a newspaper clipping from 'Express News Service' about cow urine (gomūtra) treating kidney failure in a child. This is a modern anecdotal insert by the publisher and has NO basis in classical text. It has been excluded from all database entries.
flags_and_contradictions.action: DO NOT include in any VEDA recommendation or citation

vega_dharana.title: Roganutpadanīya Adhyāya
vega_dharana.preamble: All diseases are manifested due to forceful expulsion or voluntary suppression of natural urges only.

dharaniya_vega.definition: Suppressable urges — mental and behavioral impulses that MUST be controlled

adharaniya_vega.definition: Non-suppressable natural body urges — must NOT be suppressed; satisfy immediately when they arise

suppression_diseases: Vāta-mūtra-śakṛt saṅga (retention of flatus, urine, faeces)

treatment: Special foods/drinks to eliminate obstructed faeces

suppression_diseases: All symptoms from flatus and faeces suppression
treatment: Medicated ghee internally before and after food (avapīḍaka method)
Same as treatment for hiccough (hikka cikitsā)
Tikṣṇa arka vilokana (looking at the sun)
Cold water for drinking and bathing

Food with chicken, alcohol and red śāli rice
Milk processed with drugs beneficial for urinary bladder

vega_dharana.general_treatment_principle: Since vāta is provoked by various causes everywhere, select foods and drinks to: (1) pacify vitiated doṣas, and (2) promote downward movement of vāta.

sodhana_superiority.statement: Doṣas treated with sodhana (purification) do NOT relapse. Doṣas treated only with fasting and digestive drugs may relapse. Therefore sodhana is superior to śamana.

foods: Ghṛta (ghee) — made appetizing with digestive herbs

health_criteria_disease_free_person: Adopts rules of wholesome diet and good conduct
Is patient and forgives mistakes of others
Keeps company of good, learned persons
vega_dharana.persons_not_eligible_for_treatment: Persons habituated to suppressing natural urges and suffering from complications (faecal vomiting, severe emaciation, extreme thirst, abdominal pain) are not eligible for treatment.
